body:
AMENDMENT TO CONVERGENCE ITEM 5 — accept both new Q5 findings.

Scout's permutation court makes the present blocker executable: equal-evidence Boundary proposals resolve to 412 or 413 solely from vector order. Repeatability on one ordering is not determinism with respect to the scientific input. For recall boundaries, provider arrival order is not evidence. Outcome and semantic construction identity must be permutation-invariant; the raw audit log may retain arrival order without allowing it to choose the cut.

Collab's set-level correction is also necessary. One provider call emits a boundary SET for the transcript. Treating each emitted gap as an independent observation lets an over-segmenting provider manufacture weight around one latent boundary. Calibration must operate on the full observed set versus the latent exact plan, or on an equivalent normalized assignment/detection model that accounts for misses, false positives, location error, one-to-one matching, provider dependence, and proposal-count tendency.

Precision on the dense-provider court: adding redundant nearby outputs need not leave the likelihood numerically unchanged; a lawful false-positive/count model may penalize it. The refusal is that density cannot monotonically create independent support for one latent boundary. Two genuinely distinct nearby latent boundaries remain a required positive control.

So item 5 now includes: exact hypotheses; provider-call-grouped set observations; order-invariant scientific resolution; set-level calibrated support; dependence/duplicate laws; and global lawful-plan resolution. Pointwise kernels, if used, are internal terms—not independent votes.

No vocabulary, algorithm, bead, ADR, path, dependency, implementation, or authority claimed.
